resources.string: Digital adjustments after the scan. They change the finished image, not the film or paper model. 0 = off.
Overall contrast as a tone curve on the scan. Negative flattens, positive adds punch.
Scales all colour evenly while keeping brightness and hue. −100 is black and white.
Lifts muted colours more than strong ones, so skin and skies don\'t clip.
Softens harsh fringes on very saturated colours near the edge of the gamut.
A creative warm/cool and green/magenta shift on the light entering the camera. Works on every file.
Like an 85 / 80A filter: adapts the scene to the film\'s reference light, so a tungsten stock renders daylight neutral.
Shapes the scene before it reaches the film: highlights and shadows lift or hold back their region, whites and blacks move the ends. Applied to the light, so the film still rolls it off.
A Kodak Wratten filter on the lens, changing how each colour exposes the film. The filter factor is compensated.
Blue compensation applies to Digital Intermediate output only. Off by default.
